articles.title: Strengthening Snowflake’s Distributed Query Lifecycle with Execution Anchors
articles.first_party_evidence: Snowflake domain, Engineering Blog branding, Staff Software Engineer / Engineering Manager biographies and company copyright
articles.read_scope: Introduction through Looking ahead: problem, anchor contract, normal execution, voluntary transfer, involuntary transfer, correctness, rollout, conclusion. Biographies/navigation excluded.

six_dimensions.trigger: Retries, recovery and asynchronous finalization share operation-level durable writes.
six_dimensions.failure_constraint: Multiple owners can finalize one query; ownership conventions multiply across paths.
six_dimensions.mechanism: FDB owner record, every-transaction guard, pending-write completion before voluntary transfer, durable death proof before conditional recovery claim, piggybacked acquisition.
six_dimensions.limits: Requires every durable effect to cross the guarded store; ambiguous pending-commit resolution is not described, and normal-path cost is workload-specific.
six_dimensions.counterexample: Analyst inference: unguarded external effects or a sent commit completing after timeout defeat handoff based only on local ownership.
six_dimensions.verification: Reported staged dry runs, separate rollback flags and dashboards. Proposed delayed-worker/flusher handoff and recovery-overlap probes; not executed.

evidence_sections: The core idea: An execution anchor
articles.transferable_practice: Put ownership enforcement at every durable-write boundary and test the full handoff protocol, including background work.
articles.claim_boundary: The blog reports internal design and successful rollout; no source code or independent proof was reviewed. Missing ambiguous-commit detail is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated product defect.

articles.title: TiDB Adoption at Pinterest
articles.source_type: first-party engineering account; positive design and operating constraints
articles.first_party_evidence: Official https://www.pinterestcareers.com/ footer Engineering Blog link resolves to https://medium.com/pinterest-engineering; that publication links back to Pinterest Careers. Named company engineers author the article.
articles.read_scope: Motivation through Acknowledgements: methodology, 2022 evaluation, production deployment/compute/access, offline analytics, CDC, disaster recovery, wins, learnings and next steps. Newsletter/comments/recommendations excluded.

six_dimensions.trigger: Choose a replacement distributed store for indexed, high-throughput online serving plus exports and recovery.
six_dimensions.failure_constraint: Synthetic tests miss sustained-load behavior; exports, backups and maintenance compete with serving.
six_dimensions.mechanism: Requirements filter, synthetic finalists, identical production shadow workloads, operational failure tests, learner snapshot offload and backup throttling.
six_dimensions.limits: Pinterest-specific 2022 evaluation; network remains shared, and historical competitor/CDC throughput observations are not current product facts.
six_dimensions.counterexample: Analyst inference: a synthetic winner fails if exports violate serving p99 targets; snapshot isolation can permit write skew.
six_dimensions.verification: Reported node/AZ loss, scale, termination and redeployment tests. Proposed p99/CDC-lag/RTO/RPO measurement under maintenance, snapshots, duplicate delivery and replica fallback; not executed.

articles.transferable_practice: Select infrastructure against representative traffic and failure/maintenance behavior, and budget shared resources after offload.
articles.claim_boundary: Avoid adopting historical product exclusions, speedup/cost claims or the old TiCDC throughput observation as universal guidance.

current_contract_crosschecks.title: Developer Guide — FoundationDB 7.4.8 documentation
current_contract_crosschecks.read_scope: Transactions with unknown results; The commit_unknown_result Error; Non-Retryable Errors
current_contract_crosschecks.supported_claim: An already-sent commit may succeed after timeout/cancellation. commit_unknown_result retries can repeat committed effects, requiring idempotency.
current_contract_crosschecks.qualification: A bounded wait alone is not abort proof. The Snowflake article does not disclose exact unknown-commit resolution.
